description.narrative: The project aims to contribute to long term peace in Afghanistan through strengthened local and national governance responsive to local needs on the provision of services and inclusive economic development. The project specifically aims to strengthen dialogue between government and civil society and increase the engagement of civil society in advocacy at different levels for an improvement inthe delivery of basic services by the government. This is to be achieved by linking local and national levels in policy developmentand implementation as well as effectively addressing and mitigating conflict around economic resources. In Citizens First in Afghanistan, the main strategy for influencing the local, provincial and national government is setting up andsupporting advocacy committees. These committees talk to citizens about the basic social services that are lacking in their communities. This results in a selection of demands that are raised at either the district or provincial government. When these governments don't have the authority or political willingness to respond to these demands, they are forwarded to the national government. This is the way in which the district, provincial and national advocacy committees in Citizens First cooperates. PTRO ismainly responsible for the implementation of the project activities at the district and provincial levels. Expected Program Outcomes for Afghanistan: Outcome # 2: By 2016, a number of 36 (informal) civil society organizations will have increased capacity for evidence based advocacy with district, provincial and federal level. Outcome # 3:By 2016, a total of 9 district authorities have become responsive in meeting demands from communities. Outcome # 5: By 2016, federal/national assemblies and relatedbureaucracy in both Afghanistan and Pakistan have become responsive inmeeting demands as put forward by civil society. Outcome # 6: By 2013, Increased interaction of civilian actors among Pakistan and Afghanistan to challenge existing stereotypes abouteach other.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
